# Shared interface text
**Route:** `/liivv-health/ostomy-care`  
**Source:** `core/messages/en.json` → `OstomyCare.ui`, and `chapters-data.ts`  
**Generated:** 2026-09-21 from commit `40c4e8de` — do not edit this file by hand; see [README](../README.md).

> Text that appears on more than one page: referral chips, group names, the help band, and the notices around clinical review.

## Commercial disclosure

*The paragraph at the foot of every chapter page and the funding page. Two sentences: the first always renders, the second depends on whether the page carries a clinical review. Until this pass it was one hardcoded English string — so it read in English to a French reader, and its review sentence asserted that "the information on this page was checked for accuracy against published sources" on pages whose reviewer field is deliberately empty because no review has happened. The byline and the machine-readable schema were already gated on a review existing; this paragraph now is too.*

**Always:** Liivv sells ostomy supplies. `governance.disclosure.sells`

**Where the page carries a clinical review:** Clinical review means the information on this page was checked for accuracy against published sources. It is not an endorsement of any product Liivv sells, and it is not a recommendation to buy from Liivv. `governance.disclosure.reviewMeaning`

**Where it does not — which is every page today:** Nothing on this page is an endorsement of any product Liivv sells, and nothing on it is a recommendation to buy from Liivv. `governance.disclosure.notEndorsement`

*Both halves are asserted by this export rather than protected by being unreachable: the check below fails if either locale loses the clause that says Liivv sells these products, or the clause that says nothing here is an endorsement or a recommendation to buy. That holds for the French as well, which keeping the sentence in code never did.*

## Bowel reference still — alt text, orientation and caption

- `chapter.anatomy.alt` — A drawing of the small and large intestine seen from the front, with no stoma and no pouch. The small intestine coils in the middle; the large intestine frames it, running up one side, across the top, down the other side and into a short tube at the bottom. Each number on the drawing is named in the list beside it.
- `chapter.anatomy.partsHeading` — What each number points to
- `chapter.anatomy.orientation` — Seen from the front: the right side of the body is on your left.
- `chapter.anatomy.caption` — Where a stoma is made, and whether any bowel is removed or left in place, depends on your surgery. A colostomy can be made at different points along the colon; with an ileostomy the colon may be removed or left in place. Ask your surgeon what yours means.
